We have applied template 1914393 to target molecule, got a tuple of two SMILES: product? Actually apply_template returns list of precursor SMILES. It returned "(('COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1'),)". So two precursors: "COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1" and "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1". Good.

Now need to apply template 1914394 to one of these? The order must be 1914393, then 1914394, then 1914395. Likely each step further disconnections. We need to apply 1914394 to one of the precursors that contains a Cl? The template 1914394 seems to involve a Cl-CH2-CH2? Let's inspect its retro_smarts: '[#7:3]-[C:4]-[c:5]1:[c:6]:[c:7]:[c;H0;D3;+0:8](-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[Cl;D1;H0:2]):[c:9]:[c:10]:1>>Cl-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[Cl;D1;H0:2].[#7:3]-[C:4]-[c:5]1:[c:6]:[c:7]:[cH;D2;+0:8]:[c:9]:[c:10]:1'

So it breaks a C-Cl bond to give a chloromethyl chloride? Actually forward reaction forms a C-Cl bond? The retro template splits a chloromethyl chloride from aromatic? The product side (left) is aromatic amide? The precursor side includes Cl-CH2-Cl (dichloromethane) and the aromatic amine? Our first precursor "COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1" does not have a Cl. The second "FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1" has a CCl substituent on phenyl. So apply 1914394 to that second precursor to break the CCl? Let's test matching.
